subject: ClearForge discovery follow-up: routing / auth / SLA questions
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@clearforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Apr 2024 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearForge discovery follow-up: routing / auth / SLA questions

Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so our engineering team can draft an integration runbook: 

Summary of priorities (per our call)
- Low-latency inference for interactive product editor (95th p95 target ~150–200ms for short prompts)
- Retrieval-backed summarization: 10–15 queries per user action, needs embeddings + reranker
- EU data residency for EU customers; US for US customers (we discussed region routing)
- Strict audit/log retention requirements for prod (6 months)

Clarifying questions (if you can confirm by EOD Monday it helps):
1) Which endpoints will be considered "interactive" vs. batch? (we need this for batching/cold-start config)
2) Are you able to use OAuth/OIDC for server→server auth, or do you prefer API keys scoped per-service?
3) Do you expect to pin model versions per environment (prod/stage)? Any required model families we must prioritize?
4) Who on your security team should we send the SOC2 evidence checklist to?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the feature checklist (clearforge_requirements.xlsx) — fill any missing items and we'll iterate. Ben and Dev are looped to propose a minimal routing policy and fallback chain that meets your latency/cost targets.

Next steps:
- Ben: routing & fallback proposal (technical note) — target Mon 04/08
- Dev: SDK/auth options and quickstart snippet for ClearForge — target Tue 04/09
- Alex: confirm answers to 1–4 above and share security contact

Thanks again — Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
[Attachment: clearforge_requirements.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@clearforge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Security Team <security@clearforge.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Apr 2024 09:27:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ClearForge discovery follow-up: routing / auth / SLA questions

Vanessa — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers below and a note from security attached.

Answers:
1) Interactive endpoints: editor autosuggest and single-item summarization (hard p95 target 200ms). Batch: nightly corpus re-indexing and large export jobs (no strict latency).
2) We prefer OIDC service-to-service tokens (we want short-lived credentials we can rotate). API keys okay as fallback for early POC.
3) Yes, we will pin prod to a conservative model (higher-latency but higher-fidelity). Stage can use cheaper / quantized variants. Not tied to a specific Redwood model name yet, open to your recommendation.
4) Please send SOC2 & audit docs to security@clearforge.com (I've attached a short questionnaire they completed).

One additional ask: can you propose a routing policy that routes EU traffic to EU hosts and falls back to US-only models only with customer consent? We can discuss consent flow later.

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Kim
Head of Product, ClearForge
alex.kim@clearforge.com
[Attachment: clearforge_security_q_apr2024.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@clearforge.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2024 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearForge discovery follow-up: routing / auth / SLA questions

Alex / Vanessa — looped in a technical outline. Long version below; I'll turn this into a short one-pager and a markdown proposal (attached) you can share internally.

High-level proposed plan (technical):
1) Auth / SDK
 - Recommend OIDC client credentials for prod service→service; short-lived tokens + rotation via your identity provider (we support Okta, Azure AD, and generic OIDC).
 - For POC you can use scoped API keys with usage quotas and time-limited validity.
 - SDK: server-side node/python snippets included; we'll provide an init that accepts either OIDC token or API key.

2) Model routing + policy template
 - Route by geography first: request.region (client-specified) maps to region pool. EU → eu.redwood (EU-hosted models); US → us.redwood.
 - Then select model by route priority: interactive route prefers low-latency family (rdw-gpt-lt-8k) with a cost-aware fallback to rdw-gpt-lt-q4 (quantized) if load > threshold or latency SLO starts slipping.
 - Global fallback chain: primary model → quantized variant in same region → cross-region compatible (only if customer toggles cross-region fallback) → degraded LLM (cheaper) for non-critical summarization.
 - Example policy snippet:
   - route.rule: if latency_p95_target <= 200ms then prefer rdw-gpt-lt-8k, batch.max_batch=8, kv_cache=true
   - fallback.threshold: CPU/GPU utilization > 75% OR model_queue_time > 75ms

3) Embeddings & reranker
 - Use regional embedding endpoints to keep vectors in-region.
 - Reranker as an L2/ML reranker that calls a small rerank model; can be colocated with the embedding pool. We recommend caching top-K vectors per user session (prefix caching) to reduce calls.

4) Observability & SLOs
 - Per-route telemetry: tokens, latency percentiles, model fallback counts.
 - Alert: fallback_count > 5% in 1hr for interactive route → auto-escalate to SEs.

Attachments & links:
 - Attached a short proposal (redwood-routing-proposal.md) with sample config and SDK snippets. Also adding a Drive link for a longer runbook.

Open questions for ClearForge:
 - Are you comfortable with automatic cross-region fallback if we display a short consent banner to affected users?
 - For pinned prod models: do you want automatic model rollbacks on quality regressions (we can gate by eval harness)?

Action items:
- Ben: finalize proposal doc and sample route config (target Thu 04/11) [action: Ben]
- Dev: prepare SDK quickstart with OIDC example (target Fri 04/12) [action: Dev]

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood-routing-proposal.md (MD)]

Quick internal sync and owner confirmations (keeping Alex in loop):

Ben — thanks for the detailed outline. Please prioritize the sample route config and the fallback chain example for EU→US consent scenarios. Add a short section in the doc on how we surface consent state to your client (cookie/consent API) so ClearForge can plan UX.

Dev — once Ben's config is done, spin up the SDK quickstart that demonstrates: OIDC flow (server side), client snippet for requesting region in header, and a small example showing structured output + tool calling (we'll demonstrate how to call a reranker and then a follow-up LLM for final output). Keep it as a one-file example in Node and Python.

I'll schedule a 30-min technical sync with Alex next Wed (04/17) — invite forthcoming. Please update the HubSpot deal with these action items (CF-2024-78).

Thanks — Vanessa
